newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Gold easier in Europe, traders wary of Russia news.
newsitem.headline: Gold easier in Europe, traders wary of Russia news.

text.p: Precious metals opened easier in Europe on Wednesday, with gold under pressure on talk of renewed central bank selling and platinum down on trade reports Russia would resume deliveries on July 10, dealers said.
But many traders were taking a wait-and-see approach to reports from Japanese traders that Russian authorities had informed them deliveries would resume next week.

Gold fell to $332.10/$332.60 an ounce from $333.40/$333.90 at the London close. Reports of Australian selling also weighed on prices. "In my view there has been panic selling," a dealer at a Swiss bank said, but he thought support at $330 could hold.
"I think $330 should be a floor for now. The U.S. funds are very short, and this is certainly a chance for them to cover positions," he said.
Another trader in Zurich suggested sales by a European central bank were underming gold.
"I am convinced that a central bank is selling, and this is weighing on prices," he said. Other dealers could not confirm this, but they said it could not be ruled out.
Silver eased three cents to $4.63/$4.65 in line with gold.
Platinum fell to $427.00/$432.00 from $440.50/$445.50 on the unconfirmed Japanese reports about Russian deliveries.
"We have heard time and again that Russian deliveries were about to begin, but news alone does not add liquidity to Zurich or Japan," one trader sniffed.
"There has been talk for more than a month that deliveries were coming soon," another said. "This has an impact on the market, but we just have to wait and see."
